claim.why_it_matters: The two-line column header of the integer-seconds and fractional-seconds tables in D.29.4.1 was split: its first line became a stray paragraph outside the table and the table's first column is headed only "time formats". Informative annex; no values lost.

verdict.reasoning: The claim describes the markdown accurately. On the printed page (PDF p907, printed 883) the first-column header of each table is wrapped over two lines: 'Integer-seconds' / '  time formats' and 'Fractional-seconds' / '    time formats'. The markdown keeps both words in order, directly above the table, with nothing dropped or reordered. Every format and value row in all three tables matches the print, including 'hhmmss.sssss', the leading space before '051427.8124', and 'hh:mm:ss.ssdd+hh:mm'. The difference is a wrapped header line that landed outside the table markup. That is line wrapping and formatting in an informative annex. It changes no content or meaning: the reader still sees 'Integer-seconds time formats' and 'Fractional-seconds time formats'. Under the rejection criteria (wrapping or formatting only, no change in meaning), this is not a genuine content discrepancy.
